newsitem.title: CUBA: Iraqi calls U.S. attack on Iraq a failure.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi calls U.S. attack on Iraq a failure.

text.p: A visiting Iraqi official said U.S. attacks against Iraq earlier this month served only to break an alliance of Western nations against his country, calling the action a "political and military failure".

Jasin Al Rikabi, director general of the ruling Baath party's national command, told Cuba's Communist Party daily Granma "the U.S. mission was a political and military failure, because it didn't achieve any of its objectives and it contributed to breaking the Western alliance with respect to Iraq and the Persian Gulf".
The United States should by now have realised that its own alliance had broken, given lack of support for its action from France, Saudi Arabia and Turkey, the official added.

"Iraq doesn't want war. We know the United States and its technological and military possibilities, but if they impose war on us, we will fight," said Al Rikabi, visiting Cuba since last Wednesday at the invitation of the ruling Communist Party.
"The United States maintains troops close to our borders but we can mobilise the entire people in ... hours," he added.
The Iraqi official also thanked President Fidel Castro and the Cuban people for showing solidarity towards Iraq.

Cuba, long hostile towards the United States, was quick to condemn the U.S. action, launched in early September after troops of President Saddam Hussein entered the northern part of the country to help a Kurdish faction defeat its rival in armed conflict.
At the time of the 1991 Gulf War, Cuba condemned the Iraqi invasion of Kuwait but then criticised the U.S.-led campaign against Iraq.
